title: Making Travel Arrangements
summary: We talked about booking flights and hotels and learned words for accommodation, flights and hotel services. We practised polite indirect questions, like 'Could you tell me what time the flight leaves?', in a role-play at a travel agent's.

grammar.title: Indirect questions
grammar.explain: Indirect questions are more polite than direct questions. We start with a phrase like 'Could you tell me...' and then use normal sentence word order (subject + verb). We don't use do/does/did, and for yes/no questions we add 'if' or 'whether'.
grammar.explain_ar: الأسئلة غير المباشرة أكثر تهذيباً من الأسئلة المباشرة. نبدأ بعبارة مثل Could you tell me ثم نستخدم ترتيب الجملة العادية (الفاعل + الفعل). لا نستخدم do / does / did، وفي أسئلة نعم/لا نضيف if أو whether. العبارات التي ليست أسئلة مثل I wonder و I'd like to know تنتهي بنقطة لا بعلامة استفهام.
form: Could / Can you tell me + question word + subject + verb?
Do you know + if/whether + subject + verb?
I'd like to know / I wonder + if or question word + subject + verb.
No do/does/did: What time does it leave? → ...what time it leaves

examples.en: Could you tell me when you'd like to travel?
examples.note: Direct: When would you like to travel?

examples.en: I wonder if it'd be cheaper on another date.
Can you tell me what time the flight leaves?
Do you know if that'll give me enough time?
examples.note: Direct: Will that give me enough time?

examples.en: I'd like to know if you can book me a hotel.
examples.note: Statement, so a full stop, not a question mark.

mistakes.wrong: Could you tell me what time does the flight leave?
mistakes.right: Could you tell me what time the flight leaves?
mistakes.why: Don't use 'does' in an indirect question.

mistakes.wrong: Can you tell me where is the gate?
mistakes.right: Can you tell me where the gate is?

mistakes.wrong: Do you know is breakfast included?
mistakes.right: Do you know if breakfast is included?

mistakes.wrong: I wonder if the hotel has a pool?
mistakes.right: I wonder if the hotel has a pool.
mistakes.why: 'I wonder' is a statement, so use a full stop.

quiz.q: Could you tell me how much ___?
Do you know ___ breakfast is included?
Can you tell me what the luggage allowance ___?
quiz.why: Normal order: the luggage allowance is.

options: I'd like to know if you have anything cheaper.
I'd like to know have you got anything cheaper?
I'd like to know if do you have anything cheaper.
quiz.why: if + subject + verb, and a full stop after 'I'd like to know'.

quiz.q: Direct: 'Where is the station?' Indirect: 'Could you tell me ___?'
quiz.why: The verb goes after the subject.

quiz.q: Direct: 'Can I order a vegetarian meal?' Indirect: 'Do you know ___?'
options: if I can order a vegetarian meal
can I order a vegetarian meal
if can I order a vegetarian meal

grammar.title: Present perfect simple and present perfect continuous
grammar.explain: Both tenses connect the past and the present. The present perfect simple focuses on the result or what is finished. The present perfect continuous focuses on how long an activity has been going on, and it is often still happening.
grammar.explain_ar: كلا الزمنين يربطان الماضي بالحاضر. المضارع التام البسيط يركّز على النتيجة أو ما انتهى. أما المضارع التام المستمر فيركّز على مدة استمرار النشاط، وغالباً ما زال مستمراً حتى الآن.
form: Present perfect simple: have/has + past participle (I have booked the hotel.)
Present perfect continuous: have/has + been + verb-ing (I have been waiting for two hours.)
for + a period of time (for two hours); since + a point in time (since 9 o'clock)

examples.en: I've booked the flights and the hotel.
We've been waiting at the gate for two hours.
examples.note: Still waiting: the length of time is important.
Started in the past and still happening.

mistakes.wrong: I am waiting here for two hours.
mistakes.right: I have been waiting here for two hours.
mistakes.why: For an activity from the past until now, use the present perfect continuous.

mistakes.wrong: I've been visiting Paris three times.
mistakes.why: Use the simple form to say how many times.

mistakes.wrong: I have been knowing him for years.
mistakes.right: I have known him for years.
mistakes.why: 'Know' is a state verb, so we don't use the continuous form.

quiz.q: I ___ my boarding pass. Here it is.
